sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. Appendix 5 'Kursav Grammar Sketch' pp. 883-986 (= Glottolog ref 469266); phonology sec. 5.2 pp. 887-892 (PDF 912-917); sec. 2.4.5 'Kursav Innovations' pp. 110-112. https://escholarship.org/content/qt1kj4174g/qt1kj4174g.pdf
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Kursav. Sec. 5.2 (read in full) covers consonant/vowel inventories, allophony, onset clusters with epenthetic [ɨ], diphthongs, word-final high-vowel devoicing/metathesis, /ɨ/ status, vowel elision; no stress/accent/tone statement anywhere in PDF pp. 908-1011 or sec. 2.4.5. Only stress remark in the whole work is p. 71 (Mand): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.'

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU. Faita = I4; pp. 84-88 pronoun/prefix paradigms. http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/PL-D33.pdf
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 3 p. vi: Faita shares cognates with Wanang languages, has high and mid central vowels, is 'presently dying out'; 'Isabi and Biyom languages are tonal' (not Faita). Sec. 9 p. viii-ix: semi-phonemic transcription, fluctuation table; wordlist carries no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Sec. 2.8.2.2.2.6 'The Brahman Languages' pp. 585-586. http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/PL-C38.569.pdf

sources.note: Nothing on Faita prosody; 'Faita on the Ramu River has the closest links with the Adelbert Range languages'; Biyom and Isabi 'appear to be tonal'.
